questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to lose weight quickly
Which animals have the biggest brains
How the food we eat affects our brain
Why sugar is banned in some schools
questions.why: Georgie says they'll be discussing the relationship between food and the brain.

questions.q: Why does Georgie mention eating a doughnut?
options: To show how food can quickly change our energy and mood
To recommend a healthy breakfast
To explain why she has a headache today
To show that sugar is actually good for the brain and body
questions.why: She describes a sugar rush followed by a collapse with a headache an hour later.

questions.q: Why does the brain need more fuel than other body parts?
options: It is the heaviest organ
It only works during the day, when we're awake
It uses food to grow bigger
It works 24 hours a day, even during sleep
questions.why: Phil says our brain is working 24 hours a day, even while we sleep.

questions.q: What fact about the brain does Phil give?
options: It weighs about 8 kilos
It is 2% of our weight but uses 20% of our energy
It uses 50% of the body's energy
It needs no energy at all while we are fast asleep at night
questions.why: He says the brain is only 2% of our total weight but uses 20% of the body's energy.

questions.q: What happens to Dr Reeta Achari if she doesn't eat vegetables for a day?
options: She feels very hungry all the next day
She feels less sharp the next day
She can't sleep that night
She gets a sugar rush
questions.why: She says if she doesn't eat vegetables, “the next day I'm not as sharp”.

options: Eat only one colour of food each day
Eat fruit only in the morning
Eat foods of many different colours
Avoid brightly coloured sweets
questions.why: Georgie says to eat foods of many different colours with lots of leafy greens.

questions.q: What worries Phil about the brain foods Dr Achari lists?
options: Some of them seem very expensive
They take far too long to cook at home
They don't taste good
They are hard to find in shops
questions.why: He says wild-caught Alaskan salmon is very expensive – superfoods for the super-rich.

questions.q: What is blogger Michelle Munt's view?
options: Only rich people can eat healthily
Microwave meals are the best option for busy people
Fresh food takes too long to prepare
Eating well can be cheap if you batch cook
questions.why: She says it's not expensive – you can batch cook things and freeze them for later.
